description: Operational dashboard for the event-outboxer transactional-outbox library. Filter by environment, service, pod and event type (eventType). Store-wide gauges (backlog, ages, lease count) are aggregated across pods with max; per-JVM metrics with sum. See docs/OBSERVABILITY.md in the event-outboxer repository for the full metric reference.

panels.description: Number of pods whose outbox engine reports state=running. Must equal the pod count; a drop means a crashed or stopped engine.
panels.title: Engines running

panels.description: Number of pods exposing outbox metrics at all (any engine state). Compare with 'Engines running'.
panels.title: Pods reporting

panels.description: Detected poller-thread deaths across all pods over the dashboard time range. Any non-zero value is an incident.
panels.title: Engine crashes (time range)

panels.description: PROCESSING rows abandoned past the sweep threshold and returned to PENDING by the safety-net sweeper. Any non-zero value indicates a bug or an incident.
panels.title: Stale claims swept (time range)

panels.description: Rate of failed worker heartbeats (DB connectivity) and worker registrations (restarts). Sustained heartbeat failures trigger orphan recovery from peer pods.
panels.title: Heartbeat failures / worker lifecycle

panels.description: Per-pod engine state indicator (1 = the labelled state is current). Use to find which pod crashed or is stuck stopping.
panels.title: Engine state by pod

panels.description: Event flow through the outbox, summed across pods. Sustained published > processed means the backlog is growing.
panels.title: Published / claimed / processed

panels.description: Successful finalizes per event type, summed across pods.
panels.title: Processed by event type

panels.description: How long events wait in the outbox before a worker picks them up — the end-to-end lag signal. Rising p99 means pollers or handler pools cannot keep up. Requires percentile histograms enabled on the client (management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram).
panels.title: Queue time p99 / p50 (publish → claim)

panels.description: Full processing duration per type: dispatch + lock + handler + finalize. Use for handler SLOs and to right-size handlerMaxRuntime.
panels.title: Processing time p99 by event type (claim → finalize)

panels.description: Mean processing duration (rate(sum)/rate(count)) — smoother than p99, works even without histogram buckets.
panels.title: Processing time avg by event type

panels.description: Worst single queue-time sample per pod within each scrape window. A single hot pod points at uneven claiming or a saturated executor on that pod.
panels.title: Queue time max by pod
Backlog (store-wide — aggregated with max, not sum)

panels.description: Rows in the outbox table by lifecycle status. The gauge reads a store-wide snapshot, so every pod reports the same value — aggregated with max across pods (sum would multiply by the pod count).
panels.title: Backlog by status

panels.description: Seconds since the oldest PENDING event became eligible. The primary 'am I falling behind?' alerting signal — alert when it exceeds your SLO (e.g. > 120s).
panels.title: Oldest pending age by event type

panels.description: Seconds since the oldest PROCESSING row was claimed. Early warning of a stuck handler before the watchdog force-reclaims — compare with handlerMaxRuntime.
panels.title: Oldest claimed age

panels.description: Uncaught handler exceptions, tagged with the exception class. A spike means an application bug or a downstream outage; the exception tag separates timeouts from logic errors.
panels.title: Handler errors by exception

panels.description: Retry rate split by the bounded trigger set: failure_decision (handler failed), lock_busy (contention), unknown_handler (deploy skew), dispatch_rejected (backpressure). Watch the ratio to the processed rate.
panels.title: Retries scheduled by reason

panels.description: Terminal failures: retry budget exhausted (failure_decision), a throwing failure handler (failure_handler_error), or unknown-handler policy. Any sustained non-zero value deserves triage — these rows sit in DISABLED until re-enabled.
panels.title: Events disabled by reason

panels.description: Deserialization failures (DTO schema drift, mixed-version rolling deploys) and events with no registered handler.
panels.title: Serialization errors / unknown types

panels.description: StorageException rate per storage operation (claim[TYPE], save, findDead, ...). Any sustained rate means database trouble.
panels.title: Storage errors by operation

panels.description: Events being processed right now, fleet-wide (per-JVM in-flight registries summed across pods).
panels.title: In-flight events by event type (sum across pods)

panels.description: 1 - free_capacity / capacity per pod and type. The budget is handlerPoolSize + handlerQueueCapacity (uniform for platform and virtual executors). Sustained > 0.8 means the type is close to saturation; 1.0 = pollers are parking.

targets.expr: 1 - sum by (pod, event_type) (event_outboxer_handler_executor_free_capacity{environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service",pod=~"$pod",event_type=~"$eventType"}) / sum by (pod, event_type) (event_outboxer_handler_executor_capacity{environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service",pod=~"$pod",event_type=~"$eventType"})

panels.title: Handler executor utilisation by pod

panels.description: poller.saturated = claim cycles skipped because the executor had no capacity (each increment ≈ one skipped cycle); dispatch.rejected = claims bounced off a full executor and released back to PENDING. Both signal an undersized pool.
panels.title: Poller saturation & rejected dispatches

panels.description: Share of polls that returned nothing (healthy idling when the backlog is flat; suspicious when it grows) and the average claimed batch size (consistently maxed batches with a growing backlog → raise claimBatchSize or the pool).
panels.title: Empty-poll share & claim batch size

panels.description: outcome=busy is normal contention on hot lock keys (the event is rescheduled without consuming its retry budget); outcome=error means the locker backend (Redis/PG) is failing — alert on it separately.
panels.title: Lock acquisition failures by outcome

panels.description: LockHandle.close() threw — the backend refused the release; the lock frees itself on TTL expiry. Check the locker backend.
panels.title: Lock release failures

panels.description: Rows in the lease table with an unexpired TTL. Store-wide value reported by every pod — aggregated with max. Only present with lock.type=postgres-lease.
panels.title: Live entity-lock leases (PG lease locker)

panels.description: Events reclaimed from dead workers and the number of dead workers detected. Positive values mean a peer pod crashed and the fleet took over its in-flight events.
panels.title: Orphan recovery

panels.description: Rows deleted by the opt-in retention task (archive table and old DISABLED rows). A flat line with retention enabled means the task is failing — check WARN logs.
panels.title: Retention purges by kind

panels.description: Watchdog force-reclaims of handlers exceeding handlerMaxRuntime, plus the observed stuck runtime (right axis in seconds) — use it to right-size the runtime budget.
panels.title: Stuck handlers: reclaims & runtime

panels.description: Mean attempt count recorded on processed, disabled and deleted finalizes. Values > 1 mean transient failures were recovered; a large mean = flaky handler or downstream.
panels.title: Attempts per finalized event (avg)

title: event-outboxer
